a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every pair of types X and Y, if X is nonempty, then for every system N of type S1 X Y there exists a system N′ of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N′ has a nonempty node set, and for every ordered pair of its nodes m and n there is a directed chain of one or more steps from m to n. This includes m = n, so each node must have a positive-length chain back to itself. A step from u to v means that there exist two state assignments of N′ agreeing at every node other than u, and a single input x in X, such that updating v with x gives different values for the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial assignment. (2) N′ has exactly one more node than N; it need not contain N’s nodes or preserve their updates. (3) For every finite list of inputs from X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N′ and N give equal outputs after processing the list from their respective initial assignments. There is no separate nonemptiness hypothesis on Y or on N’s node set."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every pair of types X and Y, if X is nonempty, then for every system N of type S1 X Y there exists a system N′ of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N′ has a nonempty node set, and for every ordered pair of its nodes m and n there is a directed chain of one or more steps from m to n. This includes m = n, so each node must have a positive-length chain back to itself. A step from u to v means that there exist two state assignments of N′ agreeing at every node other than u, and a single input x in X, such that updating v with x gives different values for the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial assignment. (2) N′ has exactly one more node than N; it need not contain N’s nodes or preserve their updates. (3) For every finite list of inputs from X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N′ and N give equal outputs after processing the list from their respective initial assignments. There is no separate nonemptiness hypothesis on Y or on N’s node set.

judgement.summary: For nonempty X, the TARGET defines but does not prove that every system has a twin with exactly one more unit, positive-length dependency paths between every ordered pair of units, and matching outputs on every finite input history, including the empty one. The description correctly identifies P2’s feedforward-to-recurrent direction and distinguishes the twin’s structural property from the positive ϕ claim in §2.1 and the arbitrarily high ϕ construction in Appendix A.
